title: Understanding SVD and PCA
text: In Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), a matrix X is decomposed into three matrices: U, S, and $$V^T$$. The matrix S contains the singular values, which are crucial for understanding the variance captured by each principal component in PCA.

title: Role of Singular Values
text: The singular values in matrix S indicate the amount of variance captured by each principal component. Larger singular values mean more variance is captured.

title: Reconstruction with Principal Components
text: When reconstructing a matrix using principal components, the number of components used determines the accuracy of the reconstruction. Using all components results in no reconstruction loss.
